Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

Apply the supplied format and its conditional limits
In this lesson’s supplied format, the displayed order is recipient, then premises, then locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode. Russian Post currently lists these components, but a components list is not a universal requirement to add nonexistent details. Its guidance separately discusses international addressing. The UPU country sheet includes country-before-postcode examples and an International Bureau note recommending the country on the final line for processing at origin and in transit. Thus country-before-postcode is not a universal international rule. Follow the applicable postal format and verified destination details when actually mailing. This offline lesson recognizes a supplied model; it does not verify current delivery, postal-service availability or every country’s format.

In 115114 г. Москва, г. marks the city or locality; the supplied English gloss is city. The number is a postcode, not the abbreviation being tested. The options street and building refer to different components. Read the requested abbreviation rather than treating every number or place name as the same part of an address.

In ул. Петрова, д. 14, кв. 15, the first mark ул. identifies the street. The later д. identifies the building, and кв. identifies the apartment. The supplied line thus separates street name, building number and apartment number. The answer street matches the first mark; city belongs to the locality mark and apartment belongs to the later mark. Abbreviations label address components; their positions and associated numbers help distinguish them.

The separate supplied mark д. has the English gloss building. It does not name the city or street. The line with building and apartment numbers shows why those two numbers must not be confused. These checks recognize marks in retained example lines. They do not prove that a sample address is current or deliverable, prescribe a universal postal order, or require an apartment number where none exists.

The line with building and apartment numbers shows why those two numbers must not be confused. These checks recognize marks in retained example lines. They do not prove that a sample address is current or deliverable, prescribe a universal postal order, or require an apartment number where none exists.

The retained pair к настоящему письму прилагается — enclosed please find introduces something supplied with the letter. The English gloss is a conventional correspondence expression, not a complete list of possible translations. It has an enclosure function. С уважением — Respectfully is a closing formula before the signature. An enclosure statement and a closing do different jobs: enclosed please find does not close the letter, and Respectfully does not say that a document is enclosed.

When the cue is к настоящему письму прилагается, choose enclosed please find. When the cue is С уважением, choose Respectfully. When the English cue is enclosed please find, the retained Russian match is к настоящему письму прилагается rather than С уважением. These two source-supplied pairs support recognition of enclosure versus closing, not universal formulas for every recipient or mastery of composing a complete letter. Use the retained example fragments; no new Russian sentence is required here.

The retained pair к настоящему письму прилагается — enclosed please find introduces something supplied with the letter. The English gloss is a conventional correspondence expression, not a complete list of possible translations. It has an enclosure function. С уважением — Respectfully is a closing formula before the signature. An enclosure statement and a closing do different jobs: enclosed please find does not close the letter, and Respectfully does not say that a document is enclosed.

When the cue is к настоящему письму прилагается, choose enclosed please find. When the cue is С уважением, choose Respectfully. When the English cue is enclosed please find, the retained Russian match is к настоящему письму прилагается rather than С уважением. These two source-supplied pairs support recognition of enclosure versus closing, not universal formulas for every recipient or mastery of composing a complete letter. Use the retained example fragments; no new Russian sentence is required here.

The supplied forms Вы, Вас and Вам each begin with a capital letter. The answer capital letter describes that visible initial. Minuscule means a lowercase letter; the option minuscule does not describe these displayed initials. The option plural form describes grammatical shape, not letter case. These are recognition checks, not a test of how many people a sentence addresses.

The retained grammar note describes polite address to one person using forms shared with the plural. In personal letters and official papers, a capital initial can mark respectful address to one recipient. This written convention is different from plural meaning. The same grammatical forms can address several people, so a capital initial alone does not establish the number of addressees. Identify the recipient from context, not from the English label plural form.

In the supplied respectful written-address convention, Вы, Вас and Вам have capital initials. Current Gramota guidance distinguishes respectful address to one recipient from address to several people or a general audience, where lowercase is used. A sentence-initial capital is also ordinary sentence capitalization and need not mark respectful singular address. Lowercase outside this convention is not automatically rude. Capitalization cannot be heard in speech. These checks recognize the shown letter case; choosing forms for a new letter requires recipient and genre context.

In personal letters and official papers, a capital initial can mark respectful address to one recipient. This written convention is different from plural meaning. The same grammatical forms can address several people, so a capital initial alone does not establish the number of addressees. Identify the recipient from context, not from the English label plural form.

In the supplied respectful written-address convention, Вы, Вас and Вам have capital initials. Current Gramota guidance distinguishes respectful address to one recipient from address to several people or a general audience, where lowercase is used. A sentence-initial capital is also ordinary sentence capitalization and need not mark respectful singular address. Lowercase outside this convention is not automatically rude. Capitalization cannot be heard in speech. These checks recognize the shown letter case; choosing forms for a new letter requires recipient and genre context.

recordType=meaning
sourceUrl=https://ru.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Неопределённое_местоимение&oldid=149963314
sourceRevision=149963314
sourceRecordId=neopredelennoe:==== Серия на ''-то'' ====
Местоимения данного типа выражают референтность и неи
originalSourceText===== Серия на ''-то'' ====
Местоимения данного типа выражают референтность и неизвестность говорящему (''В доме действительно кто-то был'').<br>
Местоимение на ''-то'' может употребляться также и в значении местоимения на ''-нибудь'':

: ''Но ведь кто-то должен знать?''

Кроме того, могут выполнять интродуктивную функцию:

: ''Как-то раз какой-то парень обратился ко мне с вопросом''.

==== Серия на ''-нибудь'' ====
Местоимения данной категории являются нереферентными. Значения таких местоимений определяются на основании типов контекстов и определённых семантических признаков. В случае местоимений на ''-нибудь'' одна возможность (альтернатива) рассматривается на фоне других. Такой фон возникает:
* у ситуации, отнесённой к будущему (не только грамматическое будущее время, но и, например, установка на будущее, как ''Он хочет куда-нибудь поехать летом'', или императив: ''Сделай же что-нибудь!'');
* у ситуации-альтернативы — в том числе, отнесённой к прошедшему или настоящему (например, условие (''Если она что-нибудь натворила, придётся сделать ей выговор''), эпистемическая модальность (''Кто-нибудь мог сказать ей правду!'') и др.);
* в контексте дистрибутивности (''Каждый что-нибудь с собой принесёт, За каждым произведением искусства стоит чья-нибудь история'' и т. п.).

==== Серия на ''кое-'' ====
Местоимения этой серии выражают референтный денотативный статус слабой определённости, то есть соотносятся с индивидуализированным объектом, который известен говорящему, но предполагается неизвестным слушающему. Например, ''Надо сдать кое-какие бумаги''.

sourceRecordId=neopredelennoe:==== Серия на ''-то'' ====
Местоимения данного типа выражают референтность и неи
originalSourceText===== Серия на ''-то'' ====
Местоимения данного типа выражают референтность и неизвестность говорящему (''В доме действительно кто-то был'').<br>
Местоимение на ''-то'' может употребляться также и в значении местоимения на ''-нибудь'':

: ''Но ведь кто-то должен знать?''

Кроме того, могут выполнять интродуктивную функцию:

: ''Как-то раз какой-то парень обратился ко мне с вопросом''.

==== Серия на ''-нибудь'' ====
Местоимения данной категории являются нереферентными. Значения таких местоимений определяются на основании типов контекстов и определённых семантических признаков. В случае местоимений на ''-нибудь'' одна возможность (альтернатива) рассматривается на фоне других. Такой фон возникает:
* у ситуации, отнесённой к будущему (не только грамматическое будущее время, но и, например, установка на будущее, как ''Он хочет куда-нибудь поехать летом'', или императив: ''Сделай же что-нибудь!'');
* у ситуации-альтернативы — в том числе, отнесённой к прошедшему или настоящему (например, условие (''Если она что-нибудь натворила, придётся сделать ей выговор''), эпистемическая модальность (''Кто-нибудь мог сказать ей правду!'') и др.);
* в контексте дистрибутивности (''Каждый что-нибудь с собой принесёт, За каждым произведением искусства стоит чья-нибудь история'' и т. п.).

==== Серия на ''кое-'' ====
Местоимения этой серии выражают референтный денотативный статус слабой определённости, то есть соотносятся с индивидуализированным объектом, который известен говорящему, но предполагается неизвестным слушающему. Например, ''Надо сдать кое-какие бумаги''.

sourceRecordId=neopredelennoe:==== Серия на ''-то'' ====
Местоимения данного типа выражают референтность и неи
originalSourceText===== Серия на ''-то'' ====
Местоимения данного типа выражают референтность и неизвестность говорящему (''В доме действительно кто-то был'').<br>
Местоимение на ''-то'' может употребляться также и в значении местоимения на ''-нибудь'':

: ''Но ведь кто-то должен знать?''

Кроме того, могут выполнять интродуктивную функцию:

: ''Как-то раз какой-то парень обратился ко мне с вопросом''.

==== Серия на ''-нибудь'' ====
Местоимения данной категории являются нереферентными. Значения таких местоимений определяются на основании типов контекстов и определённых семантических признаков. В случае местоимений на ''-нибудь'' одна возможность (альтернатива) рассматривается на фоне других. Такой фон возникает:
* у ситуации, отнесённой к будущему (не только грамматическое будущее время, но и, например, установка на будущее, как ''Он хочет куда-нибудь поехать летом'', или императив: ''Сделай же что-нибудь!'');
* у ситуации-альтернативы — в том числе, отнесённой к прошедшему или настоящему (например, условие (''Если она что-нибудь натворила, придётся сделать ей выговор''), эпистемическая модальность (''Кто-нибудь мог сказать ей правду!'') и др.);
* в контексте дистрибутивности (''Каждый что-нибудь с собой принесёт, За каждым произведением искусства стоит чья-нибудь история'' и т. п.).

==== Серия на ''кое-'' ====
Местоимения этой серии выражают референтный денотативный статус слабой определённости, то есть соотносятся с индивидуализированным объектом, который известен говорящему, но предполагается неизвестным слушающему. Например, ''Надо сдать кое-какие бумаги''.

sourceRevision=aa93d51920f4686153636da3dc626069acd10c893c96e07ca9dd019fe4a36218
sourceRecordId=letter:They have the same basic elements:</p>
<ol class="L1">
<li class="P14" lang="en"
originalSourceText=They have the same basic elements:</p>
<ol class="L1">
<li class="P14" lang="en">Sender’s address <span class="T12">and date</span></li>
<li class="P15" lang="en">Greeting</li>
<li class="P15" lang="en">Body</li>
<li class="P15" lang="en">Closing and signature</li>
</ol>
<p class="P11" lang="en">But there are two important differences:</p>
<ol class="L2">
<li class="P16" lang="en">Strangers and people who are not closed friends should never be addressed as “dear”.</li>
<li class="P16" lang="en">In English we begin with a topic sentence and then follow with supporting facts. In Russian the facts come first with the topic sentence as the conclusion.</li>
</ol>
<h2 class="Heading_20_2" lang="en">Greeting</h2>
<p class="RuDefinition" lang="en"><span class="T8" lang="ru">Здр</span><span class="T9" lang="ru">а</span><span class="T8" lang="ru">вствуйте!</span>—Greetings</p>
<p class="RuDefinition" lang="en"><span class="T10" lang="ru">Уважаемый</span><span class="T8" lang="ru"> Иван Иван</span><span class="T10" lang="ru">ов</span><span class="T8" lang="ru">ич</span>—Respected Ivan Ivanovich

sourceRevision=aa93d51920f4686153636da3dc626069acd10c893c96e07ca9dd019fe4a36218
sourceRecordId=letter:They have the same basic elements:</p>
<ol class="L1">
<li class="P14" lang="en"
originalSourceText=They have the same basic elements:</p>
<ol class="L1">
<li class="P14" lang="en">Sender’s address <span class="T12">and date</span></li>
<li class="P15" lang="en">Greeting</li>
<li class="P15" lang="en">Body</li>
<li class="P15" lang="en">Closing and signature</li>
</ol>
<p class="P11" lang="en">But there are two important differences:</p>
<ol class="L2">
<li class="P16" lang="en">Strangers and people who are not closed friends should never be addressed as “dear”.</li>
<li class="P16" lang="en">In English we begin with a topic sentence and then follow with supporting facts. In Russian the facts come first with the topic sentence as the conclusion.</li>
</ol>
<h2 class="Heading_20_2" lang="en">Greeting</h2>
<p class="RuDefinition" lang="en"><span class="T8" lang="ru">Здр</span><span class="T9" lang="ru">а</span><span class="T8" lang="ru">вствуйте!</span>—Greetings</p>
<p class="RuDefinition" lang="en"><span class="T10" lang="ru">Уважаемый</span><span class="T8" lang="ru"> Иван Иван</span><span class="T10" lang="ru">ов</span><span class="T8" lang="ru">ич</span>—Respected Ivan Ivanovich

recordType=meaning
sourceUrl=https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Russian_grammar&oldid=1369617627
sourceRevision=1369617627
sourceRecordId=grammar:Basic word order, both in conversation and written language, is [[subject–verb–o
originalSourceText=Basic word order, both in conversation and written language, is [[subject–verb–object]]. However, because grammatical relationships are marked by inflection, considerable latitude in word order is allowed, and all possible permutations can be used. For example, the words in the phrase "я пошёл в магазин" ('I went to the shop') can be arranged:
* Я пошёл в магазин. (I went to the shop; ''I went to the shop.'')
* Я в магазин пошёл. (I to the shop went; approx. ''I am going out, my destination is the shop.'')
* Пошёл я в магазин. (Went I to the shop; two meanings: can be treated as a beginning of a narrated story: ''"Went I to the shop, and something happened."'' or a decision made by someone after a long contemplation: ''"OK, I think I will go the shop."'')
* Пошёл в магазин я. (Went to the shop I; rarely used, can be treated as a beginning of a line of a poem written in amphibrach due to uncommon word order, or when the speaker wants to highlight that exactly this subject "went to the shop". In that case, the subject is stressed)
* В магазин я пошёл. (To the shop I went; two meanings: can be used as a response: "I went to the shop." – "Sorry, where did you go?" – ''"To the shop—that's where I went."'' or an emphasis on the way of transportation: ''I went to the shop on foot.'')
* В магазин пошёл я. (To the shop went I; ''It was me who went to the shop.'')
while maintaining grammatical correctness. Note, however, that the order of the phrase "в магазин" ("to the shop") is kept constant.

Word order can express logical stress, and degree of definiteness.
shippedText=To the shop went I

originalSourceText=Basic word order, both in conversation and written language, is [[subject–verb–object]]. However, because grammatical relationships are marked by inflection, considerable latitude in word order is allowed, and all possible permutations can be used. For example, the words in the phrase "я пошёл в магазин" ('I went to the shop') can be arranged:
* Я пошёл в магазин. (I went to the shop; ''I went to the shop.'')
* Я в магазин пошёл. (I to the shop went; approx. ''I am going out, my destination is the shop.'')
* Пошёл я в магазин. (Went I to the shop; two meanings: can be treated as a beginning of a narrated story: ''"Went I to the shop, and something happened."'' or a decision made by someone after a long contemplation: ''"OK, I think I will go the shop."'')
* Пошёл в магазин я. (Went to the shop I; rarely used, can be treated as a beginning of a line of a poem written in amphibrach due to uncommon word order, or when the speaker wants to highlight that exactly this subject "went to the shop". In that case, the subject is stressed)
* В магазин я пошёл. (To the shop I went; two meanings: can be used as a response: "I went to the shop." – "Sorry, where did you go?" – ''"To the shop—that's where I went."'' or an emphasis on the way of transportation: ''I went to the shop on foot.'')
* В магазин пошёл я. (To the shop went I; ''It was me who went to the shop.'')
while maintaining grammatical correctness. Note, however, that the order of the phrase "в магазин" ("to the shop") is kept constant.

Word order can express logical stress, and degree of definiteness.
shippedText=В магазин пошёл я.

recordType=original-synthesis
sourceUrl=urn:russian-companion:original-research-synthesis:phase3-2026-09-30
sourceRevision=phase3-2026-09-30
sourceRecordId=phase3:postal-address
originalSourceText=A complete home-delivery address names the recipient, then the premises, then the locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode.
Recipient, premises, city, and postcode alone are not the complete order. A district, oblast, krai, or republic is included when that unit applies to the locality. A federal city does not add a separate oblast line. The country names the destination state in this complete order. A post-office box replaces the street line only when that box is the delivery point, and it is not required on every street address. An apartment or office number is included only when the premises has one, and it is omitted when the premises has none.
A greeting is outside the address, and a letter convention does not identify these components.
Return to the complete order: recipient, premises, locality, applicable region, country, and postcode.
Memorizing one sample line is not the same as organizing the complete address.
Which English description identifies the city in this home-delivery address?
г. Казань
the locality names the city
Admitted reading: the locality names the city
the street line names the premises
Rejected reading: the street line names the premises
the postcode names the delivery office
Rejected reading: the postcode names the delivery office
Which English description identifies the person who receives this home-delivery address?
Анна Петрова
the addressee names the recipient
Admitted reading: the addressee names the recipient
Which English description identifies the premises in this home-delivery address?
ул. Садовая, д. 12, кв. 4
Admitted reading: the street line names the premises
Rejected reading: the addressee names the recipient
Rejected reading: the locality names the city
Which English description identifies the numeric delivery code in this home-delivery address?
420000
Admitted reading: the postcode names the delivery office
Which English description identifies a greeting that is not part of this home-delivery address?
Здравствуйте
a greeting is outside the address
Admitted reading: a greeting is outside the address
Which English description applies when only recipient, premises, city, and postcode are named?
the short sample
recipient, premises, city, and postcode alone are not the complete order
Admitted reading: recipient, premises, city, and postcode alone are not the complete order
recipient then premises then city then postcode
Rejected reading: recipient then premises then city then postcode
postcode then recipient then premises then city
Rejected reading: postcode then recipient then premises then city
Which English description identifies the regional unit that applies to this locality?
Республика Татарстан
the republic is the applicable regional unit for this locality
Admitted reading: the republic is the applicable regional unit for this locality
the republic is the six-digit postcode
Rejected reading: the republic is the six-digit postcode
the republic is a greeting outside the address
Rejected reading: the republic is a greeting outside the address
Which English description identifies the regional line for this federal city?
г. Москва
a federal city does not add a separate oblast line

originalSourceText=A complete home-delivery address names the recipient, then the premises, then the locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode.
Recipient, premises, city, and postcode alone are not the complete order. A district, oblast, krai, or republic is included when that unit applies to the locality. A federal city does not add a separate oblast line. The country names the destination state in this complete order. A post-office box replaces the street line only when that box is the delivery point, and it is not required on every street address. An apartment or office number is included only when the premises has one, and it is omitted when the premises has none.
A greeting is outside the address, and a letter convention does not identify these components.
Return to the complete order: recipient, premises, locality, applicable region, country, and postcode.
Memorizing one sample line is not the same as organizing the complete address.

originalSourceText=A complete home-delivery address names the recipient, then the premises, then the locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode.
Recipient, premises, city, and postcode alone are not the complete order. A district, oblast, krai, or republic is included when that unit applies to the locality. A federal city does not add a separate oblast line. The country names the destination state in this complete order. A post-office box replaces the street line only when that box is the delivery point, and it is not required on every street address. originalSourceText=A complete home-delivery address names the recipient, then the premises, then the locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode.
Recipient, premises, city, and postcode alone are not the complete order. A district, oblast, krai, or republic is included when that unit applies to the locality. A federal city does not add a separate oblast line. The country names the destination state in this complete order. A post-office box replaces the street line only when that box is the delivery point, and it is not required on every street address. Recipient, premises, city, and postcode alone are not the complete order. A district, oblast, krai, or republic is included when that unit applies to the locality. A federal city does not add a separate oblast line. The country names the destination state in this complete order. A post-office box replaces the street line only when that box is the delivery point, and it is not required on every street address. An apartment or office number is included only when the premises has one, and it is omitted when the premises has none.
A greeting is outside the address, and a letter convention does not identify these components.
Return to the complete order: recipient, premises, locality, applicable region, country, and postcode.
Memorizing one sample line is not the same as organizing the complete address.
Which English description identifies the city in this home-delivery address?
г. Казань

Recipient, premises, city, and postcode alone are not the complete order. A district, oblast, krai, or republic is included when that unit applies to the locality. Recipient, premises, city, and postcode alone are not the complete order. A district, oblast, krai, or republic is included when that unit applies to the locality. A federal city does not add a separate oblast line. The country names the destination state in this complete order. A post-office box replaces the street line only when that box is the delivery point, and it is not required on every street address. An apartment or office number is included only when the premises has one, and it is omitted when the premises has none.
A greeting is outside the address, and a letter convention does not identify these components.
Return to the complete order: recipient, premises, locality, applicable region, country, and postcode.
Memorizing one sample line is not the same as organizing the complete address.

A federal city does not add a separate oblast line. The country names the destination state in this complete order. originalSourceText=A complete home-delivery address names the recipient, then the premises, then the locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode.
Recipient, premises, city, and postcode alone are not the complete order. A district, oblast, krai, or republic is included when that unit applies to the locality. A federal city does not add a separate oblast line. The country names the destination state in this complete order. A post-office box replaces the street line only when that box is the delivery point, and it is not required on every street address. originalSourceText=A complete home-delivery address names the recipient, then the premises, then the locality, then the applicable region, then the country, then the postcode.
Recipient, premises, city, and postcode alone are not the complete order. A district, oblast, krai, or republic is included when that unit applies to the locality. A federal city does not add a separate oblast line. The country names the destination state in this complete order. A post-office box replaces the street line only when that box is the delivery point, and it is not required on every street address. An apartment or office number is included only when the premises has one, and it is omitted when the premises has none.
A greeting is outside the address, and a letter convention does not identify these components.
Return to the complete order: recipient, premises, locality, applicable region, country, and postcode.
Memorizing one sample line is not the same as organizing the complete address.
Which English description identifies the city in this home-delivery address?
г. Казань

sourceRecordId=neopredelennoe:==== Серия на ''-то'' ====
Местоимения данного типа выражают референтность и неи
originalSourceText===== Серия на ''-то'' ====
Местоимения данного типа выражают референтность и неизвестность говорящему (''В доме действительно кто-то был'').<br>
Местоимение на ''-то'' может употребляться также и в значении местоимения на ''-нибудь'':

: ''Но ведь кто-то должен знать?''

Кроме того, могут выполнять интродуктивную функцию:

: ''Как-то раз какой-то парень обратился ко мне с вопросом''.

==== Серия на ''-нибудь'' ====
Местоимения данной категории являются нереферентными. Значения таких местоимений определяются на основании типов контекстов и определённых семантических признаков. В случае местоимений на ''-нибудь'' одна возможность (альтернатива) рассматривается на фоне других. Такой фон возникает:
* у ситуации, отнесённой к будущему (не только грамматическое будущее время, но и, например, установка на будущее, как ''Он хочет куда-нибудь поехать летом'', или императив: ''Сделай же что-нибудь!'');
* у ситуации-альтернативы — в том числе, отнесённой к прошедшему или настоящему (например, условие (''Если она что-нибудь натворила, придётся сделать ей выговор''), эпистемическая модальность (''Кто-нибудь мог сказать ей правду!'') и др.);
* в контексте дистрибутивности (''Каждый что-нибудь с собой принесёт, За каждым произведением искусства стоит чья-нибудь история'' и т. п.).

==== Серия на ''кое-'' ====
Местоимения этой серии выражают референтный денотативный статус слабой определённости, то есть соотносятся с индивидуализированным объектом, который известен говорящему, но предполагается неизвестным слушающему. Например, ''Надо сдать кое-какие бумаги''.

* у ситуации-альтернативы — в том числе, отнесённой к прошедшему или настоящему (например, условие (''Если она что-нибудь натворила, придётся сделать ей выговор''), эпистемическая модальность (''Кто-нибудь мог сказать ей правду!'') и др.);
* в контексте дистрибутивности (''Каждый что-нибудь с собой принесёт, За каждым произведением искусства стоит чья-нибудь история'' и т. п.).

==== Серия на ''кое-'' ====
Местоимения этой серии выражают референтный денотативный статус слабой определённости, то есть соотносятся с индивидуализированным объектом, который известен говорящему, но предполагается неизвестным слушающему. Например, ''Надо сдать кое-какие бумаги''.

sourceRecordId=neopredelennoe:==== Серия на ''-то'' ====
Местоимения данного типа выражают референтность и неи
originalSourceText===== Серия на ''-то'' ====
Местоимения данного типа выражают референтность и неизвестность говорящему (''В доме действительно кто-то был'').<br>
Местоимение на ''-то'' может употребляться также и в значении местоимения на ''-нибудь'':

: ''Но ведь кто-то должен знать?''

Кроме того, могут выполнять интродуктивную функцию:

: ''Как-то раз какой-то парень обратился ко мне с вопросом''.

==== Серия на ''-нибудь'' ====
Местоимения данной категории являются нереферентными. Значения таких местоимений определяются на основании типов контекстов и определённых семантических признаков. В случае местоимений на ''-нибудь'' одна возможность (альтернатива) рассматривается на фоне других. Такой фон возникает:
* у ситуации, отнесённой к будущему (не только грамматическое будущее время, но и, например, установка на будущее, как ''Он хочет куда-нибудь поехать летом'', или императив: ''Сделай же что-нибудь!'');
* у ситуации-альтернативы — в том числе, отнесённой к прошедшему или настоящему (например, условие (''Если она что-нибудь натворила, придётся сделать ей выговор''), эпистемическая модальность (''Кто-нибудь мог сказать ей правду!'') и др.);
* в контексте дистрибутивности (''Каждый что-нибудь с собой принесёт, За каждым произведением искусства стоит чья-нибудь история'' и т. п.).

==== Серия на ''кое-'' ====
Местоимения этой серии выражают референтный денотативный статус слабой определённости, то есть соотносятся с индивидуализированным объектом, который известен говорящему, но предполагается неизвестным слушающему. Например, ''Надо сдать кое-какие бумаги''.

sourceRecordId=letter:They have the same basic elements:</p>

originalSourceText=They have the same basic elements:</p>
<ol class="L1">
<li class="P14" lang="en">Sender’s address <span class="T12">and date</span></li>
<li class="P15" lang="en">Greeting</li>
<li class="P15" lang="en">Body</li>
<li class="P15" lang="en">Closing and signature</li>
</ol>
<p class="P11" lang="en">But there are two important differences:</p>
<ol class="L2">
<li class="P16" lang="en">Strangers and people who are not closed friends should never be addressed as “dear”.</li>
<li class="P16" lang="en">In English we begin with a topic sentence and then follow with supporting facts. In Russian the facts come first with the topic sentence as the conclusion.</li>
</ol>
<h2 class="Heading_20_2" lang="en">Greeting</h2>
<p class="RuDefinition" lang="en"><span class="T8" lang="ru">Здр</span><span class="T9" lang="ru">а</span><span class="T8" lang="ru">вствуйте!</span>—Greetings</p>
<p class="RuDefinition" lang="en"><span class="T10" lang="ru">Уважаемый</span><span class="T8" lang="ru"> Иван Иван</span><span class="T10" lang="ru">ов</span><span class="T8" lang="ru">ич</span>—Respected Ivan Ivanovich
